methods.steps: `ffmpeg -i capture.avi -c:v wmv2 -c:a wmav2 archive.wmv` explicitly chooses the Windows Media Video and Windows Media Audio encoders.
methods.limits: Build must include wmv2 and wmav2; both streams are re-encoded.

methods.steps: `Image.open("badge.bmp").save("badge.ico", sizes=[(16,16),(32,32),(48,48),(256,256)])` writes a multi-size icon. By default it uses 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 128 and 256.
methods.limits: Needs Python with Pillow installed; sizes larger than the source are ignored.

methods.steps: open the CSV and review the text-import settings. Choose File > Save As, select HTML Document (LibreOffice Calc), name the output, and save. Calc exports its sheets together.
methods.limits: Review CSV import delimiter and column formats; Calc exports all sheets to HTML.

methods.steps: the documented command `csvtotable records.csv report.html` creates a standalone page. Its output offers interactive table features, so compare its presentation with a simpler document table.
methods.limits: Install utility separately; interactive standalone output differs from a simple static table. Exact input/output command documented.

methods.steps: `ffmpeg -i lecture.flv -c:v mpeg4 -q:v 4 -c:a libmp3lame lecture.avi` chooses the quality scale explicitly.
methods.limits: Requires the MPEG-4 encoder and libmp3lame; re-encodes rather than remuxes.

methods.steps: `Image.open("reaction.gif").save("reaction.ico", sizes=[(16,16),(32,32),(48,48)])` writes several sizes from one frame. The GIF loader supports seek() and tell(), so you can move to another frame before saving.
run `magick photo.jpg photo.ai`. ImageMagick's format list shows both JPEG and AI as readable and writable.
methods.limits: Build-dependent format support; the AI that results is not a traced vector drawing.

methods.steps: `ffmpeg -i interview.m4a -vn -c:a pcm_s24be interview.aiff` requests 24-bit PCM, which keeps more bits per sample than the page's output.
methods.limits: Explicit 24-bit choice does not restore previously discarded audio detail.

methods.steps: `ffmpeg -i talk.mp4 -vn -c:a libopus -b:a 96k talk.opus` sets an explicit audio bitrate.
methods.limits: Build needs libopus; -vn omits the picture.

methods.steps: open the MP4, choose File > Export Audio (Ctrl+Shift+E) and pick Opus as the format. Importing MP4 needs Audacity's optional FFmpeg library.
methods.limits: Requires the optional FFmpeg library for MP4 import.

methods.steps: first run `ffmpeg -i session.mp4 -vn session.wav`; then run `opusenc --bitrate 64 session.wav session.opus`. The intermediate WAV is an input type that opusenc documents directly.
methods.limits: opusenc does not accept MP4 directly; decode WAV first. Separate conversion programs required.

methods.steps: `ffmpeg -i broadcast.mpg -c:a libmp3lame -c:v mpeg4 -q:v 3 broadcast.avi` chooses video and audio compression directly.
methods.limits: Re-encoding, not stream-copy; build needs libmp3lame.

methods.steps: Run `ffmpeg -i camera.mxf -c copy rewrap.mov` to copy the streams without decoding or encoding.
methods.limits: No decoding or encoding; works only when the MOV container accepts the codecs inside the MXF.

methods.steps: `ffmpeg -i camera.mxf -c:v prores_ks -profile:v 2 -c:a pcm_s16le edit.mov` encodes ProRes video and PCM audio.
methods.limits: Requires the prores_ks encoder; example uses one profile and PCM.
